disc_note: 1 - lower-quartile shape correlation with the nearest neighbours (a pick lights when at least a quarter of them do not resemble it): 0 = identical, 1 = no resemblance, 2 = opposite polarity
no_value_note: picks with too few neighbours or a window with no signal to compare (RMS below 0.4 x the median) have no discontinuity

stars.rms_note: window RMS over the median window: a star with weak signal differs from its neighbours partly because noise never correlates

reference.label: interpreters' fault polygons, Hugin Fm top (2014)

truth.label: the interpreters' fault polygons on the Hugin Fm top (2014, 78 polygons), within 100 m

notes: amplitudes are relative; compare within this file only
a star is a pick whose waveform differs from its neighbours' (a fault, an edge, a pinch-out or a mis-tracked pick), not a fault as such
1 of 175558 picks left out (no trace at that inline/crossline, no pick value, or the window passes the end of the trace)
pick X/Y agree with trace X/Y (median difference 0.1 coordinate units)

Volve ST10010 PSDM full stack (3-41 degrees), depth-to-time converted, 4 ms; domain TIME and quantity AMPLITUDE as stated by the user from the text header; polarity unknown (not stated in the headers)
time-vs-depth check (seismic_lib): leans time; the cube is blank above about 204 ms (shallow mute), so its own seabed cannot be used
water bottom from the interpreters' horizons: 111 ms TWT and 91 m depth over the survey; read as time it implies 82 m of water, read as depth 111 m: only time fits

windows of +-60 ms cut at the Hugin Fm top picks smoothed over 8 bins (100 m), unaligned, so an offset across a fault shows as a changed waveform; stars = the top 3% of discontinuity, one per 60 m; stars within 150 m are joined
the fault polygons are the interpreters' own, read from the Volve interpretation files; agreement with the stars is a check, not a proof
source_label: ST10010, full stack, PSDM Kirchhoff, name ends _T
